speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help us understand what's causing the bleeding, when did these symptoms first begin, and have you noticed any joint pain or swelling along with the petechiae?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child had any recent viral illnesses, infections, or vaccinations, and have you noticed any bleeding from other sites like the ears or rectum? I would also like to know if there is any family history of bleeding disorders or if the child has been taking any new medications.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count
REQUEST TEST: Coagulation_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal); Coagulation_Panel: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal)

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal platelet count and coagulation profile, I suspect a qualitative platelet defect like von Willebrand disease. Have you noticed if the bleeding worsens with minor trauma, and is there any family history of similar bleeding issues?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Von_Willebrand_Factor_Assay
REQUEST TEST: Bleeding_Time

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal platelet count, coagulation profile, and von Willebrand factor assay, I need to rule out other qualitative platelet disorders. Does the child have any history of easy bruising since birth, or have any siblings experienced similar bleeding symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies any fever, significant weight loss, joint pains, or recent infections.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet_Function_Assay: Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors; IMAGES: Diffuse petechiae noted on forearms, legs, and trunk; mild bleeding from gums; dried blood at nares.

speaker: Doctor
text: The deficiency in GIIb/IIIa receptors confirms a diagnosis of Glanzmann thrombasthenia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
